The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
return Collections.unmodifiableCollection(
    getCredentialsInternal().getAllTokens());
```
Reason:
This line returns an unmodifiable view of the collection obtained from `getAllTokens()`. If another thread modifies the underlying collection while it is being iterated over, a `ConcurrentModificationException` will be thrown, as the iteration is not safe against concurrent modifications.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
return new ArrayList<Token<?>>(getCredentialsInternal().getAllTokens());
```
Reason:
By creating a new `ArrayList` that copies the tokens from the original collection, the modification is avoided. This ensures that the returned collection is independent of the original, thus preventing any `ConcurrentModificationException` during iteration, as the original collection can be modified without affecting the new list.
